# Git-clone-Max

> Batch clone, incrementally update, and track hundreds of Git repositories.
> Desktop app (PyQt6) for people who keep a few hundred repos around, plus
> CLI / MCP / local HTTP interfaces for agents.

## What this is

A Windows-first desktop tool that takes a list of repository URLs and clones them
in parallel, keeps them updated incrementally, and records them in a local SQLite
database with tags, statistics and health scoring. Also usable headlessly:

- **CLI** — `python -m gcm --cli --json <urls.txt>` (exit 0 all-ok / 1 some failed / 2 no valid input)
- **MCP stdio server** — read-only by default, opt in with `GCM_MCP_ENABLE=1`
- **Local HTTP API + SSE** — loopback-only, read-only by default

## Interfaces (authoritative contract)

- [`docs/agent-contract.md`](docs/agent-contract.md) — CLI/MCP/HTTP schemas, exit codes, redaction rules
- [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) — layering and data flow
- [`docs/data-model.md`](docs/data-model.md) — SQLite schema and migrations

## Skills

Six self-contained agent skill packages live under [`skills/`](skills/):

| Skill | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `gcm-clone` | Batch clone repositories, machine-readable JSON |
| `gcm-archive` | Zip snapshots of repository HEADs (no full history) |
| `gcm-diag` | Diagnose git / network / proxy readiness before cloning |
| `gcm-report` | Export repositories and sync history to CSV / Markdown |
| `gcm-resume` | Resume an interrupted batch or run incremental updates |
| `gcm-feature` | How to add a feature / command / API to this repo |

## Constraints agents must respect

- Output is redacted at the boundary. Never re-log raw tokens, credentials, or
  URLs containing userinfo — `gcm/util/redact.py` is the single implementation.
- The local HTTP API and SSE stream bind to loopback only and have **no
  authentication**. Do not expose them through a reverse proxy.
- Paid external APIs are never called for real in tests; use mocks.
- The version number has a single source: `gcm/__init__.py`'s `__version__`.
